n01.text: act3Entry: the brief gives only the entry valuation ($431M) and the four Act II contracts (90 MW). The other entry and Act II-end figures are placeholders until the save supplies them.

o01.text: Conflict: the chapter report compares net worth $512M with '$431M at entry', but $431M is also the company valuation on the Q4 2027 Plan. Founder net worth and company valuation are different fields; decide which one act3Entry scores against.

n02a.text: Signal arrows are neutral (▲ ▶ ▼ in ink), never red/green: a rising indicator is not a gain or a loss. Sparklines show past quarters only (here Q3 → Q4 2027).

n02b.text: Only Lender Spreads was read this quarter, so only it shows a band. Its 'higher means' line is the open tooltip; the other five texts live in signals_*.json, which isn't in the project yet.

n02c.text: Grey dashed blocks = reused Act II parts. Top bar adds the Signals strip and Contracts due: 3 = the H100, neocloud and AI-lab contracts ending 2028Q1–Q4.

n03.text: Read the market reads only the authored 'sharp' range in signals_*.json, never the market CSVs (doc 27 §5). The band then stays on that gauge until quarter end.

n04a.text: Renewal wall = MW by contract end quarter, from end dates only. The H100 contract is counted in GPUs and has no MW, so it's a marker, not a bar. Quarters left includes the current quarter.

n04b.text: Rent due: $104M + $72.5M + $73.6M (4,000 GPUs × $2.10 × 8,760 h, at full use) ≈ $250M/yr in the next 4 quarters. Nothing else ends in quarters 5–8, so the 8-quarter total is the same.

o04.text: Leak risk: 'comparable new-contract rate today', the nuclear PPA $/MWh ($98–165 by scenario) and the mid→top retrofit cost all come from per-scenario market files. Shown live, they tell the player which scenario they're in. Drawn as placeholders; they need a scenario-neutral source until the trigger.

n05.text: Offer = the tenant's own rate × this quarter's repricing multiplier (doc 27 §6, F-1): $104M × 0.54 ≈ $56M. Re-let: 2 quarters empty, then ~$47M/yr (≈ $1.18M/MW-yr). Counter opens Act II's negotiation modal.

o06.text: Conflict: the reopener example is a 20 MW lease signed 2027Q1, but it isn't among the Q4 2027 contracts (90 MW = 40 + 25 + 25), and the chapter report has the player sell a 20 MW site in 2027Q4. Add it to the contract list, or pick another lease for the example.

n06.text: Fee = ½ × one quarter's rent = ½ × ($44M ÷ 4) = $5.5M. Reopeners exist only on leases signed from 2027Q1, from their third year; the four Act II contracts on A3-04 don't have one.

n07.text: Sample halls: the brief gives only 120 MW energized. Assumption to confirm: a denser hall can also host older chips. Rubin NVL144's real density is >190 kW; mid tier is a documented simplification (F-3).

n08.text: Take-or-pay: you pay for the contracted MW whether the site draws them or not. Price is a placeholder (see the orange note on A3-04). Regions: PJM, Ohio, Georgia and the Nordics only (F-8).

n09.text: Only one lobbying action is specified (the coalition). The other three, the spend cards' costs and the below-15 penalty live in political_capital.json, not yet in the project: placeholders. With the director, net upkeep is +3 − 2 = +1 a quarter.

n10.text: Neither card shows a scenario, role or phase. 'Spreads Blink' body and choices are placeholder copy until events_act3.json is in the project. The Wildcard stamp is allowed: wildcards are drawn independently of the scenario.

n11.text: The only screen that names the scenario. Rival fates are illustrative game outcomes for real companies (IREN, Hut 8, Cipher); Core Scientific and CoreWeave are left out pending review (doc 27 §15).

o12.text: Conflict: the brief sets the Good preset at ~$400–450M; doc 28 (presets_act3.json) has ~$1B, flagged F-6 against Act II's accepted $412M good path. Drawn as the brief says; update presets_act3.json or the brief.

n12.text: Preset names, MW, debt, rating and summaries are placeholders until presets_act3.json is in the project. Scenario Mode names the scenarios openly: allowed, because it unlocks only after finishing Act III.
